text:
vivian: Quick follow-up from the autoscaler RFC — we need to settle grace periods and where the deployment/operator boundary should enforce them.
raj: +1 need something concrete. current behaviour (soft_scaledown then hard) is surprising to tenants.
hao: We should separate two concerns: eviction safety (avoid killing in-flight requests) and capacity accounting (headroom/credits). Different TTLs make sense.
maria: Agreed. Proposal: soft_grace = per-VM short window (e.g. 60s) for transient load dips; hard_grace = longer (e.g. 10m) before we actually return capacity to the pool.
sam: How do we handle operator handoff? If control plane decides to scale down but operator is mid-drain, we should extend hard_grace automatically.
vivian: Operator should expose a drain_state API. Control plane can query: { currently_draining: bool, draining_until_ts: 12345 }. If draining, respect draining_until + safety_margin.
raj: That requires a synchronous call from autoscaler to operator. Any perf concerns? high QPS on operator endpoints?
hao: Keep it eventual: cache the drain_state for 5s. For scale-down decisions use cached state; for immediate emergency drains we can do a forced-sync.
maria: Also need a clear config surface. Example: 
```
autoscaler:
  soft_grace_seconds: 60
  hard_grace_seconds: 600
  drain_cache_ttl_seconds: 5
  drain_safety_margin_seconds: 30
  prewarm_headroom_pct: 0.12
  eviction_ttl_minutes: 30
```
sam: prewarm_headroom_pct needs to be per-tenant or per-pool? big tenants might want static reservation.
vivian: We'll support tenant-level overrides in dedicated pools. Default is pool-level.
raj: For burst lanes — we should allow temporary credit borrowing that counts against hard_grace. Example: tenant A borrows 2 GPUs for 3m; autoscaler should prefer revoking credits before evicting instances.
hao: Implementation note: track credits as a separate ledger. When scale-down candidate selected, first try to reclaim credits, then nodes with lowest utilization.
maria: Metrics to surface in console: soft_scale_count, hard_scale_count, delayed_scale_actions, average_drain_time. Those help debug why capacity wasn't returned.
autoscaler-bot: [info] pool/dedicated-prod scaled down candidates=3 reclaimed_credits=1 at 2765432145
vivian: Edge case: rolling upgrades where control plane triggers a version bump — we must not combine scale-down with upgrade eviction. Suggest a simple circuit: if rolling_upgrade_in_progress -> freeze hard_grace enforcement until upgrade completes.
sam: Sounds reasonable but document the risk: could temporarily increase capacity spend.
raj: One more: backoff behavior when oscillation detected. Use exponential backoff on scale-down decisions, but allow immediate scale-up. Backoff state should be per-pool not global.
hao: Proposed backoff algo: if scale-down reversed within 2x hard_grace -> double next hard_grace up to 4x cap. Reset after stable window of 30m.
maria: I'll draft a follow-up RFC section with config keys, operator handshake proto, and a short test plan (unit tests + chaos sim for drains).
vivian: Awesome. Can we also add a short-lived CLI to inspect drain_state and credit ledger? would help debugging.
raj: :+1: ping me when draft is ready, I can run through the test scenarios.
vivian: Thanks all — action items: maria will write RFC addendum, hao will sketch operator endpoint, sam will document tenant overrides.
autoscaler-bot: [reminder] next autoscaler sync scheduled at 2765432200
